title: Requirement Revisions and Standard Editions
purpose: Define immutable requirement revisions, immutable Standard editions, independent maturity and disposition, compatibility semantics, and the externally anchored bootstrap and successor-validation process.
scope: This specification covers revision coordinates for stable requirements; edition labels for frozen specification sets; publication maturity and disposition; Semantic Versioning classification including explicit pre-1.0 compatibility declarations; immutable edition provenance; bootstrap validation; successor cross-validation; conformance corpora; human behavioral review; and governance claims.
context: Requirement editing, specification publication, and review maturity are separate concerns. Keeping their coordinates independent lets authors continue work while consumers remain pinned to exact immutable contracts and lets a self-hosted Standard establish trust without relying on circular self-certification.

requirements.title: Keep requirement identity stable across refinement
requirements.statement: A requirement MUST retain its stable `REQ-...` identifier when an edit refines the same obligation.

requirements.title: Assign immutable requirement revisions
requirements.statement: A system assigning or importing requirement revisions MUST create a new positive integer revision for every accepted edit, keep prior content recoverable, preserve a supplied positive revision for immutable imported content, and never derive the normative revision from a provider storage or concurrency version.
notes: Normative requirement revision and provider concurrency coordinates are independent even when their numeric values happen to match.

requirements.title: Address exact requirement content
requirements.statement: A reference that depends on exact requirement content MUST identify both the stable requirement ID and its revision.
notes: A bare requirement ID intentionally means the requirement across revisions.

requirements.title: Create a new ID for a different obligation
requirements.statement: A fundamentally different obligation MUST receive a new requirement ID and explicit lineage such as `supersedes` or `derived_from`.

requirements.title: Freeze specification sets as editions
requirements.statement: A published specification set MUST freeze its ordered artifacts and exact requirement revisions in an immutable edition manifest.
notes: Commits and ordinary edits do not automatically create editions.

requirements.title: Use Semantic Versioning for editions
requirements.statement: A Standard edition MUST use a Semantic Versioning label with only the `draft.N` and `rc.N` prerelease forms defined by this specification.
notes: Draft example: 0.1.0-draft.1. Candidate example: 0.1.0-rc.1. Stable example: 0.1.0.

requirements.title: Classify breaking edition changes
requirements.statement: A breaking change to accepted content, stable identifiers, trace meaning, canonicalization, or required behavior MUST increment the major edition component after 1.0.0.
notes: Before 1.0.0, a breaking change increments the minor component and resets patch to zero, and the manifest declares compatibility as breaking.

requirements.title: Classify backward-compatible additions
requirements.statement: A backward-compatible normative addition MUST increment the minor edition component and reset patch to zero.
notes: During 0.x this rule applies only when the addition is actually backward-compatible; breaking 0.x editions use the explicit exception in `REQ-VER-0007`.

requirements.title: Reserve patch editions for non-normative corrections
requirements.statement: A patch edition MUST preserve normative interpretation and validation behavior.
notes: A correction that changes accepted content or observable validator behavior is not a patch.

requirements.title: Declare pre-1.0 compatibility
requirements.statement: Every 0.x edition manifest MUST declare whether its change is breaking, backward-compatible, or non-normative relative to its predecessor.
notes: The bootstrap edition has no predecessor and records `bootstrap: true` instead.

requirements.title: Record independent publication maturity
requirements.statement: An immutable edition manifest MUST record exactly one maturity value of `draft`, `candidate`, or `stable` independently of its edition number.
notes: Stable means supported under the named publisher governance and does not imply external standards-body ratification.

requirements.title: Keep maturity consistent with prerelease labels
requirements.statement: Edition validation MUST require `draft` with `-draft.N`, `candidate` with `-rc.N`, and `stable` with no prerelease suffix.
notes: The explicit maturity field prevents consumers from inferring governance solely from a version string.

requirements.title: Keep publication disposition outside the immutable manifest
requirements.statement: Publication administration MUST model `active`, `superseded`, and `withdrawn` as mutable disposition outside the immutable edition digest.
notes: A disposition transition records actor, time, reason, and successor where applicable without rewriting edition bytes or maturity.

requirements.title: Record edition provenance
requirements.statement: An edition manifest MUST record governance, source commit and path, payload, model-schema, and edition-manifest-schema hashes, canonicalization, exact requirement revisions, conformance-corpus hash, validator results, approval reference, and signature reference.

requirements.title: Anchor the bootstrap edition externally
requirements.statement: The first published edition MUST set `bootstrap` to true and derive trust from independently reproducible schema validation, review evidence, hashes, and a signed tag or release manifest.
notes: A candidate implementation declaring its own output valid is not sufficient bootstrap evidence.

requirements.title: Validate bootstrap bytes independently
requirements.statement: Bootstrap validation MUST include ordinary JSON Schema validation and at least one small validation implementation independent of the candidate SpecAttest validator.

requirements.title: Require documented human bootstrap review
requirements.statement: Bootstrap publication MUST include a completed human review checklist covering identifiers, revision coordinates, normative language, schemas, hashes, known gaps, and governance approval.
notes: The checklist is evidence about the frozen bytes rather than a substitute for machine validation.

requirements.title: Cross-validate successor editions
requirements.statement: A non-bootstrap candidate edition MUST be checked by the last accepted validator, the candidate validator, and the shared conformance corpus.
notes: Validator result records pin the validator versions and result hashes.

requirements.title: Review successor behavioral differences
requirements.statement: A non-bootstrap candidate edition MUST include human review of behavioral differences between the accepted and candidate validators.
notes: Differences are either reconciled, documented as intended compatibility changes, or treated as publication blockers.

requirements.title: Publish immutable draft editions without consensus claims
requirements.statement: A publisher MAY publish an owner-governed immutable draft edition when its maturity, governance, provenance, and known gaps are explicit.
notes: Draft publication provides a stable integration target without claiming broad consensus.

requirements.title: Pin consumers to exact editions
requirements.statement: A conforming consumer MUST support pinning to an exact edition manifest and its payload digest rather than treating a branch head as an edition.
notes: Development can continue on the canonical branch while consumers remain pinned.

requirements.title: Separate requirement identity from provider concurrency
requirements.statement: An interchange or authority-transfer implementation MUST preserve the stable requirement ID and exact normative revision while carrying provider storage, project, and operation concurrency coordinates separately.

requirements.title: Make safe-mutation replay deterministic
requirements.statement: A safe-mutation implementation MUST compute its idempotency digest from caller-controlled logical input after deterministic normalization and exclude server-generated timestamps, identifiers, and other defaults.
notes: Replaying the same logical request and idempotency key produces the same digest even when omitted operational timestamps receive different server values.

requirements.title: Keep normative and concurrency revisions distinct in safe mutation
requirements.statement: A safe-mutation envelope MUST represent normative requirement `revision`, `expectedProjectVersion`, and `expectedOperationVersion` as distinct coordinates with no implicit conversion among them.

requirements.title: Preserve atomic authority transfer behavior
requirements.statement: A safe-mutation authority transfer MUST require an idempotency key and expected versions, reject stale state without partial mutation or automatic merge, and make commit, cancel, and resume retries deterministic.
notes: The protocol contract is transport-neutral; REST and MCP bindings expose equivalent observable outcomes.
